newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to make it easier to market terminal equipment.
newsitem.headline: EU to make it easier to market terminal equipment.

text.p: The European Commission, preparing for fully liberalised telecoms markets next year, put forward a proposal on Friday designed to make it easier to bring new terminal equipment into the fast-growing market.

"When implemented, the new framework will speed up the time taken to bring new equipment onto the market and will extend the single European market to all types of radio and wire-based telecommunications terminals," the Commission said.
"A fast and flexible framework which relies on self- certification by industry, rather than cumbersome testing by outside bodies is proposed," it added in a statement.

The EU executive said the proposed legislation met the changing needs of the market caused by the explosive growth of mobile services and the full liberalisation of the supply of telecommunications networks and services from January 1998.
A much lighter regulatory regime could be put in place given technological progress, liberalisation and reduced product life cycles, it said.

The directive -- which includes all terminal equipment -- would bring with it a reduced and flexible set of requirements that products must meet and the replacement of third party testing of equipment with manufacturers' declarations.

"Regulation is minimised for new types of terminal so that innovative services can be deployed as quickly as possible and the requirements placed on all types of terminal can be relaxed in the light of the experience," it said.
